title: Ragan R
content: I had surgery on July 31, 2020. It was a very difficult experience in the hospital. I was alone due to Covid restrictions and my husband was not allowed to stay with me. I felt neglected and was mocked for being in pain. They did not feed me for 40 hours because they wanted to discharge me to free up the bed. I was told I could only have ibuprofen. I moaned in pain for five hours while nurses belittled and laughed at me. I would never have believed it if I hadn't experienced it myself. Finally, a nurse brought me crackers and grapes that she paid for herself. I checked in the morning of July 31 and left late at night the next day, August 1. I cannot be sure exactly when the event happened, but I believe it was during one of the first two nights at home. It was definitely sometime between August 1 and 4, 2020. I was on pain medication, but I could not tolerate it well because it made me nauseous. I was in a lot of pain. In the middle of the night, I suddenly woke up but could not move my body. I was trapped. It did not feel like a dream. I was alert and awake. I could hear my husband next to me, snoring. I felt like I stayed there for a minute or two, just wondering why I couldn’t control my body. Then I began to slowly rise into the air. It was a slow and very smooth ascent. At first, I did not understand what was happening and simply experienced the feeling of levitating. Then I looked down and saw my body and my husband’s body on the bed. That is when the experience became worrisome. I wondered why my husband wasn’t waking up as I floated toward the ceiling, and I grew concerned. Then I actually reached the top of the ceiling. I tried to push myself down. There was something over my left shoulder, a presence that I could not see. It was telling me not to worry and to relax. That is when I became frantic and started pushing down harder, arguing, "No! I have to stay with my kids!" I was actually speaking aloud. The other being did not use words; we communicated through thought. I was not in a good situation with my husband. He was not sober, and my children were both in elementary school. I greatly feared what would happen if I were not there with them. My parents lived four hours away. So I kept fighting to push myself down and said, "No!" I did not float back down. Rather, I was instantly back in my body. And then it was just over. The presence was gone. I could move again. I woke my husband up, and he thought I was crazy or high on pain medication. Since I never took more than one and a half pills every six hours, that was not the case. I have never experienced anything else like it. I saw a view from my tray ceiling that I had never seen before. I noticed a small place on the wall where the paint was damaged. I stood on my bed and looked up there a couple of weeks later, and it was just as I remembered. It was not a dream. It felt just like being awake. I can tell the difference between a dream and waking life.

arrival.other_being_detail: A presence over her left shoulder that she could not see; it communicated through thought and told her not to worry and to relax.

stage_sequence.sequence_variation_description: She awoke unable to move, then slowly rose/levitated to the ceiling, saw her body and her husband in bed, sensed an unseen presence communicating reassurance, argued to return for her children, and was instantly back in her body.

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: Episode occurred at home after surgery while on pain medication and included sleep-paralysis-like onset (awake but unable to move) followed by smooth levitation to the ceiling.
unique_elements.notable_quotes: "No! I have to stay with my kids!"; "It was not a dream. It felt just like being awake."
